title: I Admitted I Was the Asshole About the Parking Swap

parts.text: I took the covered spot I had traded, then pretended the trade had expired. I am thirty-eight, tired dad, Civic, rain. My neighbor Hasan had swapped me his covered spot for a week while my kid was sick, so I would not soak the car seat. Week ended. Rain did not. I stayed covered and told myself he would understand. He did not. He knocked, polite, with a dripping hoodie. The hoodie smelled like wet cotton and patience running out. I almost performed a story about permits. I looked at Mateo in the window and felt the cheapness of the story. I moved the Civic. I baked nothing as apology because that is not my skill. I wrote a note: you were right, I was protecting a seat and calling it a child's fever. Hasan texted thanks and a thumbs up. I am the asshole. The uncovered spot splashed my jeans the next morning, correctly. I tell this because AITA is not always a debate club. Sometimes it is a dripping hoodie. Hasan said, "Week's up, man" I said, "You're right. I'm moving it now" Mateo asked why we moved. I said because we had a deal. I can still name the ugly little detail, which is how I know it happened.

social.video_title: I kept the covered spot after the deal ended
social.description: A sick kid is not a forever permit. The dripping hoodie was the whole verdict. Would you have moved the car in the rain?
